oewn-08197108-n.learner: ordinary people in general, taken all together.
examples: The new law was meant to give more power to the people.

oewn-08507209-n.learner: the country, state or city where you live.
examples: His home is Chicago, but he works in New York.

oewn-08094856-n.learner: a group of people who live together as one unit.
examples: The whole home was up early, from the grandparents to the baby.

oewn-08602685-n.learner: the place where something started and then grew strong.
examples: Italy is the home of opera.

oewn-03533280-n.learner: a place where people who need care are looked after.
examples: Her grandfather moved into a home for the elderly.

connotation.why: softer word than 'institution'; 'put in a home' can sting

oewn-08507412-n.learner: the place where you are based, where your missions start and end.
examples: The ship's home is a port in Virginia, and every voyage starts and ends there.

oewn-03534081-n.learner: in baseball, the rubber slab where the batter stands, which a runner must touch to score.
examples: He slid into home just ahead of the throw.

oewn-08077878-n.learner: a company that trades or makes goods, together with the people who make it up.
examples: She runs a small business that sells bread.

oewn-00583425-n.learner: the main work you do in your life to earn money.
examples: He has been in the building business for twenty years.

oewn-01098150-n.learner: how much buying and selling is going on.
examples: Business was slow at the shop this week.

oewn-07983541-n.learner: companies and firms, taken all together as a group.
examples: Government and business could not agree on the new tax.

oewn-08418511-n.learner: customers, taken all together as a group.
examples: The new cafe across the street took away much of our business.

oewn-00551378-n.learner: small extra actions an actor does on stage to add to the drama.
examples: His business with the cane made the whole audience laugh.

oewn-08540894-n.learner: the part that is roughly in the middle of a larger area.
examples: Their hotel was in the heart of the city.

oewn-07560035-n.learner: a warm feeling of liking someone or something.
examples: The puppy soon won everyone's heart.
After the third defeat, the team began to lose heart.

oewn-04632183-n.learner: a leaning or tendency of a certain kind.
examples: He had a change of heart and decided to stay.

oewn-13888525-n.learner: a flat shape whose rounded sides curve in at the top and meet in a point at the bottom, as used on playing cards and valentines.
examples: She drew a heart at the bottom of the birthday note.

oewn-03512192-n.learner: a playing card of the hearts, a major suit, with one or more red heart shapes on it.
examples: She played a heart and won the trick.

oewn-07667514-n.learner: an animal's heart eaten as meat, which is firm and rather dry and usually comes from a cow or calf.
examples: The butcher sold us a beef heart for the stew.

oewn-02620422-v.learner: to have a certain kind of life, or to live in a certain style.
examples: they will settle so quietly, and live in so rational a manner
After the war they had to live very simply.

oewn-02624202-v.learner: to stay alive and not die.
examples: The doctors doubted she would live, but she got better.

oewn-02621023-v.learner: to go after a full and satisfying life.
examples: Stop working all the time and start to live!

oewn-00598039-v.learner: to know a state, situation, feeling or sensation because you have been through it yourself.
examples: She had lived that fear herself as a child.

oewn-11438252-n.learner: the unknown, unpredictable thing that makes an event turn out one way rather than another.
examples: Whether we win or lose is now up to fortune.

oewn-00614532-v.learner: to leave something behind without meaning to.
examples: I forgot my umbrella on the train.

oewn-04764777-n.learner: doubt about whether something is true, real, or exists.
examples: There is no question that she told the truth.

oewn-07176710-n.learner: an informal way of talking about asking someone to marry you.
examples: He finally popped the question over dinner.

oewn-07178244-n.learner: a formal suggestion for action put to a meeting or council, to be discussed and voted on.
examples: The chair put the question to a vote.

oewn-00735067-v.learner: to find the solution to something.
examples: She resolved the puzzle in ten minutes.
Scholars have never fully resolved what the poem's last line means.
The stronger lens resolved the tiny cells on the slide.

oewn-00448264-v.learner: to make a substance go into a solution, as when it dissolves in a liquid.
examples: The heat slowly resolved the salt into the water.
The baby had a bad night and woke four times.

oewn-15194806-n.learner: a short word for nightfall, the time when it gets dark.
examples: We must reach the village before night.
The rider vanished into the night.

oewn-15192624-n.learner: a time of ignorance, of being backward, or of gloom.
examples: The country slowly came out of its long night of war and fear.

connotation.why: casts a period as dark, ignorant or backward
